The story follows a clear, logical progression structured around the academic calendar and the escalating phases of the building's renovation. Every element—from the specific academic specialties of the characters (such as Arthur’s focus on "the Aesthetics of Ruin" and fragments) to the bureaucratic jargon of the administration—serves to reinforce the central themes of institutional decay and scholarly endurance. The beginning sets up the ironic premise (fixing a leak makes the building exponentially less habitable), the middle escalates the physical and psychological toll on the faculty, and the climax (the catastrophic March flood) logically leads to the characters' resigned acceptance at the end. The thematic interplay between high-minded literary theory and the gritty, physical reality of construction creates a harmonious, unified, and darkly comedic whole.
